412	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
413	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
414	
415	Make Vertical Version makes a tall or square version of a landscape edit, for a phone, a reel or a square post. It changes the canvas and reworks the whole timeline in one step, so you don't have to frame each clip yourself.
416	
417	<AtAGlance
418	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
419	  tools="make_vertical_version"
420	  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
421	/>
422	
423	## Make a vertical version
424	
425	<Steps>
426	
427	1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. It's available when the project has a clip, no [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, no other sheet is up and nothing is recording.
428	
429	2. Pick a [**Shape**](#shape).
430	
431	3. Choose what to [**Follow**](#follow), and set [**Zoom**](#zoom) and [**Where Empty**](#where-empty) if you want to.
432	
433	4. Leave [**Make a copy**](#make-a-copy) ticked to keep this project as it is, or untick it to change this project.
434	
435	5. [Read the summary](#read-the-summary) under the controls. It says what will happen before anything does.
436	
437	6. Choose **Make** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.
438	
439	</Steps>
440	
441	<Shot
442	  name="15j-make-vertical-sheet.sheet"
443	  alt="The Make Vertical Version sheet, with Shape on 9:16 (540 × 960), Follow on Subject, Zoom at 100 %, Where Empty on Show Whole and Make a copy ticked. The summary under them reads: Makes a 540 × 960 version. Keeps 4 clips as placed."
444	/>
445	
446	Each clip is treated by what it is: full-frame movies follow their subject, screen recordings follow the pointer, camera layouts are laid out again, and so on. [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) goes through it clip by clip.
447	
448	## The controls
449	
450	### Shape
451	
452	Each row shows the size it makes, such as **9:16 (1080 × 1920)**. The new canvas keeps the old short side, rounded down to an even number, and the height follows from the shape.
453	
454	| Shape | From 1920 × 1080 |
455	| --- | --- |
456	| **9:16** | 1080 × 1920 |
457	| **4:5** | 1080 × 1350 |
458	| **1:1** | 1080 × 1080 |
459	
460	A shape the canvas already has isn't in the list.
461	
462	### Follow
463	
464	What each movie clip keeps in the frame.
465	
466	| Choice | What the frame follows |
467	| --- | --- |
468	| **Subject** | A face. Where there's no face, a person. Where there's neither, the region the eye goes to. |
469	| **Faces** | Faces only. |
470	| **People** | People only. |
471	| **Salient Region** | Only the region the eye goes to. |
472	| **Speaker** | Whoever is talking, for a wide shot with a microphone per person. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/). |
473	| **Center** | The middle of the picture, for the whole clip. Needs no analysis, so the summary is ready at once. |
474	
475	These are the choices of [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), plus **Speaker**. The two commands share one remembered choice, saved when you choose **Make**. It starts on **Subject**. If you last chose **Speaker**, Follow Subject, which doesn't offer it, opens on **Subject**.
476	
477	### Zoom
478	
479	How tight the frame is, from 100 to 400 %, in whole numbers. 100 % is the smallest scale at which a picture covers the new canvas. Higher values frame closer.
480	
481	**Zoom** starts at 100 % each time you choose the command and isn't remembered. The one exception is the sheet that [comes back after a Speaker analysis](/framing/follow-speaker/#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis), which keeps what you set. The summary updates when you leave the field.
482	
483	### Where Empty
484	
485	What a followed clip shows while there's nothing to follow.
486	
487	| Choice | What the frame shows |
488	| --- | --- |
489	| **Show Whole** | The whole picture on a blurred copy of itself. This is the default. |
490	| **Center** | The middle of the picture. |
491	
492	It's dimmed while **Follow** is **Center**. It's the same remembered choice as Follow Subject's.
493	
494	### Make a copy
495	
496	Ticked, the vertical version opens as a new untitled project and this project doesn't change. The copy is named after this project with the shape, such as "Interview (9:16)", "Interview (4:5)" or "Interview (1:1)". It carries the project's caches and analysis. Save it when you want to keep it.
497	
498	Unticked, this project itself becomes the vertical version.
499	
500	The box is ticked each time you choose the command, and your choice isn't remembered. Only the sheet that comes back after a Speaker analysis keeps what you chose.
501	
502	## Read the summary
503	
504	Under the controls, the sheet says what **Make** will do, and it changes as you change a control. It opens with the new size, "Makes a 1080 × 1920 version.", and goes on with whichever of these apply:
505	
506	| The summary says | What it means |
507	| --- | --- |
508	| "Follows 3 clips." | Every clip that's followed, so it includes the clips the next two rows count. |
509	| "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced." | Screen recordings that follow the pointer. |
510	| "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip." | Wide shots framed on the speaker. |
511	| "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas." | Camera layout switches made again. |
512	| "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." | Clips with nothing to follow at any point. |
513	| "Keeps 4 clips as placed." | Clips moved and scaled to the new canvas, not framed. |
514	| "Re-fills 1 background." | Blurred copies and background plates resized to cover the new canvas. |
515	| "Removes 1 blurred copy the framing replaces." | Old blurred copies that are no longer needed. |
516	| "Re-sizes 1 graphic to the new canvas." | Graphics exactly the old canvas's size. |
517	| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | Older copies of a bundled template, in a copy only. |
518	| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | A new track at the back for the blurred copies. |
519	| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | A further track, for copies that overlap in time. |
520	| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions a clip already had, so each was split there and eased again on either side. |
521	| "2 actions carry a framing move." | A framing move couldn't fit between a clip's own actions, so those actions carry it. |
522	| "Re-lays 1 caption track for the new canvas." | Word captions paged again for the narrow frame. |
523	
524	After those come single lines for what needs your attention:
525	
526	- One line per camera layout switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."
527	- One line per clip that isn't followed, or is only partly followed, with the reason: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." or "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found."
528	- One line per caption track that's kept as it was, and one per graphic module left as it is.
529	
530	If the movies have already been analysed, the summary reads "Reading the analysis…" for a moment, and **Make** is dimmed until it's done.
531	
532	If Frame Job can't make the new version, the summary says why and **Make** stays dimmed. When an analysis has to run first, Frame Job beeps after it instead and says why at the foot of the inspector. A project at its limit of 64 tracks, nests included, is one such case, because Make Vertical needs a track for the blurred copies.
533	
534	## When the movies need analysing
535	
536	Following a subject needs to know where the faces, people and shot changes are. When the movies haven't been analysed yet, the summary says so: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."
537	
538	**Make** then shows the Analyzing sheet while that runs on your Mac, and makes the version when it's done. **Stop** makes nothing: no project opens and this one doesn't change.
539	
540	**Center** needs no analysis, and a recording that follows its pointer is never analysed. With **Speaker**, the sheet comes back after the analysis so you can [confirm who is on each microphone](/framing/follow-speaker/#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis).
541	
542	If an analysis fails, Frame Job beeps, makes nothing and names the file at the foot of the inspector.
543	
544	## Make another shape
545	
546	What was found stays in this project's cache and is carried into the copy, so making another shape afterwards needs no analysis. Choose the command again on the landscape project and pick the next shape.
547	
548	## Undo Make Vertical
549	
550	The whole change is one undo step. In the copy, **Edit ▸ Undo Make Vertical** gives back the landscape edit. In place, it takes the command back on this project.
551	
552	## Keep the picture sharp
553	
554	A vertical canvas shows part of a landscape picture enlarged. A 1080p source framed on 1080 × 1920 is enlarged ×1.78, which can look soft on a phone, and a **Zoom** above 100 % enlarges it further. Shoot 4K for footage you mean to make vertical.
555	
556	## Good to know
557	
558	- Make Vertical works on the top-level timeline. A [nest](/editing/nests/) is treated as one clip, and what's inside it isn't reframed.
559	- If the project changes while the sheet is open or the analysis runs, nothing is made. Frame Job beeps and the foot of the inspector says "the project changed while the Make Vertical Version sheet was open, so nothing was made. Choose Make Vertical Version again." or "the project changed while Make Vertical was analyzing, so nothing was made. Choose Make Vertical Version again."
560	- If the step wouldn't change the copy, the copy is closed and nothing is made: "Make Vertical did not apply to the copy, so nothing was made."
561	
562	## With an agent
563	
564	[`make_vertical_version`](/mcp/tools-framing/#make_vertical_version) makes the same version from a named shape. It differs from the sheet in a few ways:
565	
566	- It can save the copy straight to a place you choose, and the assistant asks first when it does.
567	- It can leave caption tracks as placed, where the sheet always pages them again.
568	- It waits up to 60 s for an analysis. Past that nothing is made, and calling it again carries on.
569	- It takes **Zoom** as 1 to 4 rather than a percentage.
570	
571	See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

7	
8	[Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) doesn't crop the timeline as one picture. It looks at each clip and treats it by what it is, so a talking head follows its subject while a title stays a title. This page says what happens to each kind of clip, and what the sheet's summary says about it.
9	
10	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…" tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']} />
11	
12	## How a clip is judged
13	
14	Every clip with a picture on the top-level timeline is judged on the old canvas. The first row that fits decides what happens to it.
15	
16	| The clip | What happens |
17	| --- | --- |
18	| A [blurred copy](#blurred-copies-and-background-plates) behind a clip | Removed, or re-filled to cover the new canvas |
19	| A [background plate](#blurred-copies-and-background-plates) | Re-filled to cover the new canvas |
20	| A [graphic exactly the old canvas's size](#graphics) | Re-sized to the new canvas |
21	| A [camera or a screen in a camera layout](#camera-layouts) | Laid out again for the new canvas |
22	| A [screen recording with its cursor file](#screen-recordings) that fills the frame | Follows the pointer |
23	| A [movie](#full-frame-movies) that fills the frame | Follows its subject |
24	| A [still, picture or nest](#stills-pictures-and-nests) that fills the frame | Centred |
25	| [Word captions](#word-captions) | Paged again for the narrow frame |
26	| [Everything else](#everything-else) | Kept as placed |
27	
28	A clip **fills the old frame** when its rectangle at its first frame covers the canvas on one side, to within a pixel at each edge, and on the other side is centred to within 2 % or covers that too. So the usual full-frame shot counts, and so does one punched in a little. A picture-in-picture doesn't.
29	
30	A sound-only clip, a clip with its video turned off and an adjustment clip have no picture here, so nothing happens to them.
31	
32	## Full-frame movies
33	
34	A movie clip that fills the old frame follows what you chose in **Follow**, as [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) frames it. Its own moves and actions stay, inside the framing.
35	
36	Where the frame shows the whole picture, a blurred copy of the clip goes behind it, so the canvas around it isn't empty. The copies go on a new **Backgrounds** track at the back, and copies that overlap in time go on further tracks behind it. The track is removed when no copy needs it.
37	
38	The summary tells you how each one went:
39	
40	| The clip | The summary says |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| Follows its subject | It's counted in "Follows 3 clips." |
43	| Has nothing to follow at any point | It's counted in "Shows 1 clip whole on a blurred copy." |
44	| Has nothing to follow for part of its length | It's still counted as followed, with "Clip 2 is followed, but it is shown whole on a blurred copy where no subject is found." |
45	| Moves by a [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) of its own | "Clip 2 is followed, but moves by its own motion: …", with the preset's name, because that move isn't part of the framing. |
46	
47	Some movies can't be followed and are kept as placed, each listed with the reason:
48	
49	- A movie whose file is missing: "Clip 6 is not followed: its media file is missing, so it is kept as placed." With **Follow** on **Center** it's centred like any other clip instead.
50	- A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), or one a matte cuts, because framing would move it out of the matte.
51	- A clip turned by its rotation or by an action, or one that spins in its motion, because framing works on an upright picture.
52	
53	With **Follow** on **Speaker**, a wide shot beside its microphones cuts to whoever is talking, and every other movie follows its faces. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
54	
55	## Screen recordings
56	
57	A screen recording with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) follows the pointer instead of a face, because a face on a screen isn't what the viewer is looking at.
58	
59	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when it strays from the middle of the frame, by more than 20 % of the frame's width or 12 % of its height.
60	- It arrives on a click outside that area. The move ends on the click's frame, so the click lands in view.
61	- It holds still while you type.
62	- Any zoom and pan of the clip's own, such as [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/)'s, is replaced, since the tall frame is already a close-up. The summary says so: "Follows the cursor in 2 clips, their own zooms and pans replaced."
63	
64	**Where Empty** doesn't apply to a recording that follows its pointer. **Center** centres the recording as any other movie.
65	
66	When the cursor file can't be read, because it was moved or deleted, the recording is shown whole on a blurred copy and the summary says "its cursor file could not be read, so it is shown whole".
67	
68	## Camera layouts
69	
70	A screen recording and its camera in [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) keep their arrangement. This covers the layouts of **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** and the layout a recording landed in. Each switch is made again for the new canvas, at the same time, length and curve.
71	
72	| On the old canvas | On the new canvas |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| A Corner | A Corner in the same corner |
75	| Camera Full | Camera Full |
76	| Side by Side, going to a tall canvas | Stacked, with the screen across the top and the camera below it, so the screen isn't squeezed into two-thirds of a narrow frame |
77	| Side by Side, going to a square | Side by Side |
78	
79	The camera, the screen and the cut pieces of either are never followed and get no blurred copy. A zoom on the screen keeps showing the same part of the picture.
80	
81	The summary counts them, "Re-lays 2 camera layouts for the new canvas.", and lists each switch: "Re-laid: Side by Side → Stacked at 00:00:10:00."
82	
83	A circle or panel crop is re-centred on the middle of the crop it had. A crop that had room to move may sit nearer the middle of the camera picture than a switch made directly on the new canvas would.
84	
85	### A layout changed by hand
86	
87	If a camera's position, crop or corner radius changed by more than a pixel after its switch, or its scale or opacity by more than 0.001, it's no longer a layout Frame Job made. The camera and its screen are kept as placed, and the summary says "Clip 6 is not followed: its camera layout was edited by hand, so it is kept as placed."
88	
89	## Stills, pictures and nests
90	
91	A still or a picture that fills the frame is centred, and so is a [nest](/editing/nests/) that does. There's nothing inside them to follow. The summary lists each one: "Clip 4 is not followed: it is a still picture, so it is centred." or "Clip 4 is not followed: it is a nest, so it is centred."
92	
93	What's inside a nest isn't reframed. A still, picture or nest that doesn't fill the frame is [kept as placed](#everything-else).
94	
95	## Graphics
96	
97	A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, such as a full-frame lower third or title card, is re-sized to the new canvas, so it lays itself out again on the narrow frame. Its position, and the positions its actions move it to, shrink and stretch with the two sides. Its scale stays as it was. Any other graphic is [kept as placed](#everything-else).
98	
99	Older copies of the bundled templates in the project are updated in a copy, and listed when you apply the step in place: "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height is listed too, and never rewritten. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).
100	
101	## Everything else
102	
103	Titles, other graphics, shapes, a picture-in-picture and any clip that doesn't fill the frame are kept as placed. They're moved and scaled from the old canvas to the new one, as the Document tab does when a [canvas change](/projects/canvas-size/) rescales clips:
104	
105	- A clip's horizontal position follows the change in width.
106	- Its vertical position follows the change in height.
107	- Its scale follows the smaller of the two changes, so something that fitted the old canvas still fits the new one.
108	
109	From 1920 × 1080 to 1080 × 1920, a title's distance from the centre shrinks to 0.56 across and grows to 1.78 down, and the title itself shrinks to 0.56 of its size. The positions and scales its actions move to change the same way.
110	
111	## Blurred copies and background plates
112	
113	A blurred copy already behind a clip is removed when that clip is framed, because the framing makes a new one where it's needed. Otherwise it's re-filled to cover the new canvas. A copy counts as one when it's named **Blurred Background** and a clip of the same source, start and length sits in front of it.
114	
115	A background plate from **Clip ▸ Add Background** is re-filled too. A plate is a rectangle shape the canvas's size, centred at scale 1, or an image or still named **Background** that fills the canvas. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
116	
117	## Word captions
118	
119	Word captions are split into pages again for the narrow frame, from the words their pages already hold, as **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas** does. Every correction you typed is kept, but the new pages are drawn fresh from the style, so a colour or position you changed on a page goes. A track that was hidden or locked stays that way. See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/).
120	
121	A caption track that can't be re-laid is kept as placed, and the summary names it: "Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings." That happens to [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/), and to a track when:
122	
123	- it's a matte track
124	- a page has no word timings, or none of a page's words starts inside it
125	- a page is in a style Frame Job doesn't make, or its pages are in more than one style
126	- its pages wouldn't fit
127	
128	## With an agent
129	
130	[`make_vertical_version`](/mcp/tools-framing/#make_vertical_version) tells the agent how each clip was treated and why, which clips followed their pointer, and each layout switch it made again. It can also leave caption tracks as placed, where the sheet always pages them again. [`reframe_clip`](/mcp/tools-framing/#reframe_clip) applies one of these framings to a single clip. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
131

141	title: Follow the speaker in a vertical
142	description: Make a vertical version of a wide interview that cuts to whoever is talking, using a microphone per person.
143	---
144	
145	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
146	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
147	
148	A wide shot of two to four people doesn't fit a tall frame. Follow Speaker solves that: in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/), it reads each person's microphone and cuts the frame to whoever is talking.
149	
150	<AtAGlance
151	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
152	  where="Follow ▸ Speaker in the sheet"
153	  tools={['make_vertical_version', 'reframe_clip']}
154	  needs="A microphone for each person, on its own track. Faces are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
155	/>
156	
157	## What you need
158	
159	- A wide shot: a full-frame movie clip with the people in it.
160	- A sound file for each person, from a recorder or a lavalier rather than a camera, each on its own track and recorded with the shot.
161	- Those sound files lined up with the shot. Use [**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**](/audio/synchronize-audio/) first.
162	
163	## Follow the speaker
164	
165	<Steps>
166	
167	1. Choose **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** and set **Follow** to **Speaker**. The **Microphones** and **Faces** rows appear.
168	
169	2. Under [**Microphones**](#microphones), tick the tracks that belong to the people in the shot, two to four.
170	
171	3. Under [**Faces**](#faces), check that each row names that microphone's person. If the movies haven't been analysed yet the pop-ups have no faces for now.
172	
173	4. Choose **Make**. If an analysis has to run first, [the sheet comes back](#the-sheet-comes-back-after-analysis) when it's done, so you can do step 3 and choose **Make** there.
174	
175	</Steps>
176	
177	The other controls work as they do in [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/#the-controls).
178	
179	## Microphones
180	
181	A checkbox for each track holding a sound file, named by the track and listed front to back. Sound from a movie file doesn't count, so a camera's track isn't offered, and neither is a track whose clips all have their sound off. The first four are ticked.
182	
183	Tick the ones that belong to the people in the shot. **Make** needs two to four, so with more than four tracks listed, check which four are ticked.
184	
185	When no full-frame movie plays beside two ticked microphones, the sheet says "No full-frame movie clip plays beside two of the ticked microphones, so nobody can be framed by who is talking." and **Make** stays dimmed. Check that the shot and the microphones overlap on the timeline.
186	
187	## Faces
188	
189	One row per ticked microphone, with a pop-up of the faces Frame Job found in the longest shot it can frame this way. Faces are numbered left to right, with where each sits across the picture: **Face 1 (42 % across)**.
190	
191	Ticking or unticking a microphone rebuilds the rows and offers the match again for the new set. Otherwise your own choice stands.
192	
193	### The automatic match
194	
195	Frame Job matches each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. When the match is clear the pop-ups are already set, and the note under them reads "Each microphone is matched to the face that talks with it; change one if it is wrong." Check that each row names that microphone's person.
196	
197	A match is clear when every microphone agrees with its face to at least 0.2, on a scale where 1 is perfect agreement and 0 is none. A face is counted when it's in at least a quarter of the shot, and four faces at most are considered.
198	
199	### Choose a face
200	
201	When the match isn't clear, each pop-up says **Choose a face** and the note reads "The faces do not show clearly who is on each microphone: choose each microphone's face." Pick each microphone's face yourself.
202	
203	If the shot shows fewer faces than the ticked microphones under it, the pop-ups have no faces to offer. Untick the microphones of people who aren't in it.
204	
205	## When Make is offered
206	
207	**Make** is available when all of these are true:
208	
209	- Two to four microphones are ticked.
210	- A full-frame movie plays at the same time as at least two of them.
211	- Every ticked microphone has a face of its own. Two microphones can't share a face.
212	
213	While an analysis is still to be made there are no faces to choose yet, so the last rule waits: **Make** is available with the first two, and choosing it runs the analysis.
214	
215	A microphone imported moments ago may still be being measured. The sheet says so in the words [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) uses, such as "The microphone on track 3 is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet. Try again in a moment." Choose the command again in a moment. A microphone with no speech under the shot stops **Make** in the same way, with "The microphone on track 3 has no speech between …". Untick it.
216	
217	## The sheet comes back after analysis
218	
219	The summary warns you first: "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 3 files on this Mac first, then asks you to confirm who is on each microphone, then makes a 1080 × 1920 version."
220	
221	When you choose **Make**, the Analyzing sheet runs. Then the sheet comes back on the same shape, **Follow**, **Zoom**, **Where Empty**, **Make a copy** and ticked microphones, this time with faces to confirm. Nothing is made until you choose **Make** there. **Stop** on the Analyzing sheet makes nothing.
222	
223	## How the shot is cut
224	
225	A shot is framed this way when it's a full-frame movie, its file is present, it has no cursor file, it isn't on a microphone track, and it overlaps sound on at least two ticked microphones. Frame Job doesn't count the people in it. The summary counts these shots: "Follows whoever is talking in 1 clip."
226	
227	Who talks when is read the way Switch by Speaker reads the microphones, with its default settings, so the two agree.
228	
229	- Each change of speaker is a cut, not a move.
230	- Each framing holds at least 2 s, so a short reply doesn't cut away and back.
231	- Two people talking at once are framed together when they fit. When they don't, the frame stays on one of them, the one already in it if that person is talking.
232	- While nobody talks, the last speaker stays.
233	
234	Every other movie clip follows its faces, and screen recordings and everything else are treated as usual. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
235	
236	## Shots that follow their faces instead
237	
238	A shot that can't be framed by who is talking follows its faces instead, and the summary says why: "Clip 3 is followed, but it follows its faces, not who is talking, because …". The reasons include:
239	
240	- It changes shot. Follow Speaker frames one wide shot, so split the clip first with **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**.
241	- It shows fewer faces than the microphones under it.
242	- Nobody talks inside it on those microphones.
243	
244	## Good to know
245	
246	- The faces you confirm come from the longest shot and apply to every shot by number, counting left to right. If people sit in a different order in another shot, that shot frames the wrong person.
247	- A shot uses only the ticked microphones that sound under it, so a microphone used elsewhere in the timeline doesn't count against it.
248	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) doesn't offer **Speaker**. Only Make Vertical Version and an agent do.
249	
250	## With an agent
251	
252	An agent makes the same version with [`make_vertical_version`](/mcp/tools-framing/#make_vertical_version), naming two to four microphone clips, each standing for its track, and the faces if it wants to set them. Nobody confirms a match, so a shot whose faces don't show who is whose follows its faces unless the call names them, and the agent is told why. It's also told which microphones and faces each shot used. [`reframe_clip`](/mcp/tools-framing/#reframe_clip) frames one clip on whoever is talking, on the canvas it's already on. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
253	
254	## Related
255	
256	- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
257	- [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
258	- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
259	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
260	- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)

262	title: Camera layouts
263	description: Switch a screen recording and the camera in front of it between corner, side-by-side, stacked and full-frame layouts as it plays.
264	---
265	
266	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
267	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
268	
269	A camera layout decides how a camera clip and the screen recording behind it share the frame. Choose one at any moment and the picture eases into it there, so a tutorial can go from a small corner camera to a full-frame talking head and back as it plays.
270	
271	<AtAGlance
272	  menu="Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸"
273	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Layout"
274	  tools="switch_layout"
275	/>
276	
277	## Switch the layout
278	
279	<Steps>
280	
281	1. Move the playhead to where the switch should start.
282	
283	2. Tell Frame Job which clips to use. With nothing selected it looks for the track named "Camera", which is where a recording's camera lands, so usually there's nothing to do. Otherwise select the camera, or the camera and the screen. See [Which clips](#which-clips).
284	
285	3. Choose a layout from **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**.
286	
287	</Steps>
288	
289	To change layout again later, move the playhead on and choose another. To undo a switch, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd>: one undo step, **Camera Layout**, takes the whole switch back. These items have no keyboard shortcut.
290	
291	The [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/) in the inspector does the same thing for one selected clip, with a switch length you choose. To start a recording in a layout, [choose it in the recorder panel](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/#choose-a-layout) before you record.
292	
293	## The layouts
294	
295	The submenu holds **Corner ▸**, **Rounded Corner ▸** and **Circle ▸**, each with **Bottom Right**, **Bottom Left**, **Top Right** and **Top Left**, then **Side by Side**, **Stacked**, **Camera Full** and **Screen Only**.
296	
297	In the three corner layouts, Camera Full and Screen Only, the screen goes to its full placement. That's where **Add Clip** puts a new clip: centred, and scaled down to fit when it's bigger than the canvas and **Fit new clips to canvas** is on in the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). A screen smaller than the canvas isn't scaled up.
298	
299	### Corner
300	
301	The camera shows its whole picture, with square corners, in the corner you choose. It's fitted inside a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third tall, 5 % in from the canvas's edges. This is the box a recording's camera lands in by default.
302	
303	### Rounded Corner
304	
305	The same box with rounded corners, the radius 8 % of the box's shorter side.
306	
307	### Circle
308	
309	The largest square of the camera's picture, cropped to a circle in the corner you choose. The circle is as wide as the box's shorter side, so on a 16:9 canvas it's a third of the canvas's height, and it sits 5 % in from the edges.
310	
311	### Side by Side
312	
313	The screen is fitted in the left two-thirds and the camera is cropped to fill the right third. There's a margin of 4 % of the canvas's shorter side around and between them, and both have their corners rounded by 2 % of that side. It needs a screen.
314	
315	### Stacked
316	
317	The screen runs across the top, centred, and takes up to two-thirds of the height inside the margins. The camera is cropped to fill the rest below it. The margins and corners are the same as Side by Side's. It needs a screen, and it works on any canvas, not only a tall one.
318	
319	### Camera Full
320	
321	The camera fills the canvas, with square corners. It's scaled until no canvas shows, so a picture of another shape runs off two edges.
322	
323	### Screen Only
324	
325	The camera is hidden where it is, its opacity going to 0, and the screen goes to its full placement. The camera clip keeps playing, so its sound carries on.
326	
327	## Which clips
328	
329	Frame Job works out the camera and the screen from the selection and the playhead. They don't have to come from a recording: any clip with a picture can be the camera, and any clip with a picture behind it can be the screen.
330	
331	| Selected | The camera | The screen |
332	| --- | --- | --- |
333	| Two clips with a picture, on different tracks | The front one | The other one |
334	| One clip with a picture | That clip | The clip drawing behind it at the playhead |
335	| Nothing | The clip at the playhead on the front-most track named "Camera" | The clip drawing behind it at the playhead |
336	
337	The clip drawing behind the camera is the front-most one playing at the playhead on a track behind the camera's. Frame Job passes over hidden tracks, [matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/), [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) and clips with their picture switched off.
338	
339	With no screen, the corner layouts, Camera Full and Screen Only lay out the camera alone. Side by Side and Stacked won't.
340	
341	The items are dimmed when:
342	
343	- the camera doesn't play at the playhead. A selected clip the playhead isn't on doesn't fall back to the "Camera" track
344	- three or more clips are selected, or two on one track
345	- a selected clip has no picture of its own, such as a text clip, an adjustment clip or a sound-only clip
346	- a sheet is open
347	
348	The menu works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/). There, the nest's canvas is the canvas and the "Camera" track is the one inside the nest.
349	
350	## The switch
351	
352	A switch eases from the old layout into the new one over 0.5 s from the playhead. It's a layout action on each clip, so you can see it on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and retime it like any other action. Each action sets position, scale, crop, corner radius and opacity.
353	
354	- **At a clip's first frame** it cuts instead of easing. The layout becomes the clip's own placement there, and a one-frame action marks the cut. Each clip is judged on its own, so a camera that starts at the playhead cuts while the screen behind it eases.
355	- **Near an end** the switch is shortened to finish by the clip's end or the clip's next layout action, and it's never shorter than one frame.
356	- **While another layout is still easing,** the first one ends where the second begins.
357	- **Where a layout action already starts,** the new layout replaces it.
358	
359	## How far a layout reaches
360	
361	A layout holds until the next switch, so a camera cut into pieces stays in the corner.
362	
363	Every later clip with a picture on the camera's track, and on the screen's, that starts before the next layout action on that track takes the layout as its own placement, with no easing. With no later switch, that runs to the end of the track. Each track's reach is worked out separately.
364	
365	Those later clips keep their own actions, though an action that moves one can [stop the switch](/framing/layout-section/#a-layout-meets-a-zoom). Because a later clip takes the layout as its placement, removing the layout action afterwards doesn't put that clip back. Use Undo for that.
366	
367	## When a switch is refused
368	
369	A switch that can't be made changes nothing. Frame Job beeps, and [the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip) shows the reason after "Refused:". The numbers in it are Frame Job's own ids for the clip and the action, and the timecode is when that clip starts or, in the first two rows, the playhead.
370	
371	| The inspector says | What it means |
372	| --- | --- |
373	| "clip 12 does not play at 00:00:04:10" | The clip isn't under the playhead. Move the playhead onto it. With two clips selected, this can be the screen. |
374	| "no clip draws behind clip 12 at 00:00:04:10 to be the screen" | Side by Side or Stacked found no screen. Pick another layout, or put a clip behind the camera. |
375	| "clip 12 is a nest clip, which cannot draw a rounded corner or a circle." | A nest clip shows square corners only, so a nest can't take Rounded Corner or Circle as the camera. That goes for a later camera clip in the layout's reach too. Use Corner. |
376	| "The screen clip 8 at 00:00:00:00 zooms (action 10); nest the screen's clips…" | The clip holds a zoom or another moving action after the playhead. See [A layout meets a zoom](/framing/layout-section/#a-layout-meets-a-zoom), which also covers the sheet Frame Job usually offers here. |
377	| "action 10 on clip 8 already runs from …, and two actions on one clip may not overlap" | Two actions on one clip can't overlap, and the switch's span runs into another action, such as a volume change. Move the playhead, shorten the switch in the [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/), or move that action. |
378	
379	## Good to know
380	
381	- A layout sets position, scale, crop, corner radius and opacity on both clips, replacing what you'd set by hand. Rotation and everything else stay as they were.
382	- A nest clip in Side by Side or Stacked keeps square corners.
383	- Side by Side stays side by side on a tall canvas if you choose it there. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) is what re-lays your switches for a new shape, and it turns Side by Side into Stacked on a canvas taller than wide.
384	- The camera's crop in Circle, Side by Side and Stacked can [centre on the person](/framing/layout-section/#the-crop-centred-on-the-person) instead of the picture.
385	
386	## With an agent
387	
388	[`switch_layout`](/mcp/tools-framing/#switch_layout) does what the menu does, at any time rather than the playhead. An agent can also:
389	
390	- name the camera and the screen itself. The screen must be on a track behind the camera's, and each must have a picture and play at that time
391	- set how long the switch takes and how it eases, where the menu always eases in and out over 0.5 s
392	- stop a layout holding at a time of its choosing, with no later switch
393	- switch inside a nest without opening it, where that nest's canvas is the canvas. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/)
394	
395	See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/). An agent can also choose a recording's layout when it [records](/mcp/record-screen/).
396

412	
413	The Layout section is the inspector's way to make a [camera layout](/framing/camera-layouts/) switch. It lays out the selected clip as the camera and, unlike the menu, lets you choose how long the switch takes.
414	
415	<AtAGlance
416	  menu="Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸"
417	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Layout"
418	  tools="switch_layout"
419	  needs="Nothing for a layout. A crop centres on the person only when Remove Background has already made the camera's masks, on your Mac."
420	/>
421	
422	<Shot
423	  name="05j-clip-layout.inspector"
424	  alt="The Picture sub-tab scrolled to the open Layout section, its summary reading Square, Bottom Right. Layout is set to Corner, Shape to Square, Corner to Bottom Right and Duration to 0.50 s, with the Switch at Playhead button underneath."
425	/>
426	
427	## Switch at Playhead
428	
429	<Steps>
430	
431	1. Select the camera clip, and only that clip. It needs to be a clip of a video file with a picture. An image, a still or a nest gets no Layout section, though [the menu](/framing/camera-layouts/#which-clips) can lay one out.
432	
433	2. Open **Layout** in the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab. It comes after Transform and Behind Subject, and it's shut until you open it.
434	
435	3. Set the [controls](#the-controls).
436	
437	4. Move the playhead onto the clip, to where the switch should start.
438	
439	5. Press **Switch at Playhead**.
440	
441	</Steps>
442	
443	This does exactly what **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** does, with this clip as the camera and the clip drawing behind it as the screen. It's one undo step, **Camera Layout**. Everything in [The switch](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-switch) and [How far a layout reaches](/framing/camera-layouts/#how-far-a-layout-reaches) applies.
444	
445	The button is off while a sheet is open. Pressed with the playhead off the clip, the foot of the inspector says the clip doesn't play there and nothing changes.
446	
447	## The controls
448	
449	| Control | What it does | Default | Choices |
450	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
451	| **Layout** | The layout to switch to. | Corner | Corner, Side by Side, Stacked, Camera Full, Screen Only |
452	| **Shape** | The corner picture's shape. Square is the menu's **Corner ▸**, Rounded its **Rounded Corner ▸**. Greyed for any layout but Corner. | Square | Square, Rounded, Circle |
453	| **Corner** | Which canvas corner the camera sits in. Greyed for any layout but Corner. | Bottom Right | Bottom Right, Bottom Left, Top Right, Top Left |
454	| **Duration** | How long the switch takes. | 0.5 s | 0.01 to 10 s |
455	
456	The section's header sums up what it would switch to: "Square, Bottom Right", or "Side by Side".
457	
458	Type a **Duration**, or pick 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 from the arrow in the field. A typed number outside the range goes to the nearest end of it. The switch is then rounded to whole frames, and a length under half a frame rounds to nothing, so Frame Job shows an error and doesn't switch. That's 0.01 s on a 30 fps project. At a clip's first frame the switch cuts, whatever the Duration.
459	
460	These choices belong to the section, not to the project. They stay while the window is open, they aren't saved and they aren't undo steps, so nothing changes until you press **Switch at Playhead**. There's no Reset.
461	
462	## The crop centred on the person
463	
464	Circle, Side by Side and Stacked crop the camera. When the camera's person masks already exist for every frame the clip plays, the crop centres on the person, at the middle of where the masks find them, averaged over the clip. This works from the menu and the section alike.
465	
466	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) makes the masks, on your Mac, and they stay in the project's cache. You can turn Remove Background off again afterwards. A layout never starts that analysis itself. With no masks, or masks for only part of the clip, the crop centres on the picture. A camera that's an image clip centres on the picture, masks or not.
467	
468	Frame Job reads the masks for a moment before it switches. If the project changes in that moment, it beeps and makes no switch. Choose the layout again.
469	
470	## A layout meets a zoom
471	
472	A switch never fights a zoom. Frame Job won't switch when a clip it would move holds a zoom or another moving action after the playhead, because the two would pull the clip in different directions.
473	
474	A moving action is any action that changes position, scale, crop, corner radius or opacity, other than a layout action. On the clip under the playhead, only an action that ends after the playhead counts, so moving the playhead past the end of a zoom clears the way. On a later clip in the layout's [reach](/framing/camera-layouts/#how-far-a-layout-reaches), any moving action counts.
475	
476	There's one exception. In Corner, Camera Full and Screen Only, a screen still at its [full placement](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-layouts) stays where it is, so its zooms keep playing and the switch goes ahead. Side by Side and Stacked always move the screen.
477	
478	When a nest would let the switch go ahead, Frame Job offers one. Otherwise the foot of the inspector names the clip and the action, and nothing changes. To make the switch anyway, move the playhead past the end of that action if it's on the clip under the playhead, or [remove the action](/motion/change-an-action/#remove-an-action), then switch again.
479	
480	## Lay out the clips in a nest?
481	
482	This sheet shows the reason the switch couldn't be made, then offers to put those clips in a [nest](/editing/nests/) first. The layout then moves the nest, and the zoom keeps playing inside it.
483	
484	- **Nest and Switch** makes the nest and the layout. One undo step, **Camera Layout**, takes both back.
485	- **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> changes nothing.
486	
487	What goes in the nest is the clip at the playhead and the later clips in the layout's reach, apart from a clip that holds the next switch. Only the side that stopped the switch is nested, so a screen that zooms is nested and its camera isn't. If both the camera and the screen hold a moving action, each gets a nest of its own.
488	
489	There's no offer when:
490	
491	- one of those clips is already laid out, because a nest would lay it out twice. That includes a clip that sits anywhere but its [full placement](/framing/camera-layouts/#the-layouts), such as a camera a recording landed in the corner
492	- the camera holds the moving action and you chose Rounded Corner or Circle, because a nest clip shows square corners only
493	
494	When the camera itself goes into a nest, its crop centres on the nest's picture rather than the person.
495	
496	## With an agent
497	
498	An agent is never shown the sheet. It asks for the nest in the same [`switch_layout`](/mcp/tools-framing/#switch_layout) call, and Frame Job won't do that when one of the clips is already laid out.
499	
500	An agent can also centre the camera's crop on a point of its own choosing, and that point stays as sent even when the camera goes into a nest. If it doesn't choose one, the crop is filled from the masks as it is for the menu, and the call's answer gives the centre it used. See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
501

511	description: How an agent frames one clip on the canvas, from following a face, a pointer or whoever is talking to rescaling it from an older canvas.

513	
514	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
515	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
516	
517	`reframe_clip` is how an agent fits one clip to the current canvas, say a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 canvas. The agent can be the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/) or [one you connect yourself](/mcp/overview/). [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) frame clips the same way, and this page is for when you want an agent to do it one clip at a time, with every choice in its hands.
518	
519	<AtAGlance
520	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
521	  tools={['reframe_clip', 'set_canvas', 'undo']}
522	  needs="Nothing to set up. Faces, people and salient regions are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
523	/>
524	
525	## Frame a clip
526	
527	<Steps>
528	
529	1. Set the [canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) you want, because the frame is worked out for the current canvas. An agent does this with `set_canvas`, leaving `rescale_clips` off. Inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas.
530	
531	2. Ask the agent to frame the clip and say what to follow, for example "follow the face in this clip". It calls `reframe_clip` with the `clip` and what to `follow`, and everything else is optional:
532	
533	   ```json
534	   { "clip": 12, "follow": "face", "zoom": 1.5 }
535	   ```
536	
537	3. If the agent says the clip is [still being analysed](#waiting-for-analysis), have it call again.
538	
539	4. Play the clip back. **Edit ▸ Undo Reframe Clip** takes the whole framing back.
540	
541	</Steps>
542	
543	A framing that would leave the clip exactly as it is changes nothing, and the agent is told the project is already in that state. There's no undo step for it. [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/#reframe_clip) lists every argument.
544	
545	## Choose what to follow
546	
547	| `follow` | What the frame does | Analysis |
548	| --- | --- | --- |
549	| `subject` | Follows a face, else a person, else a salient region | Yes |
550	| `face`, `person`, `salient` | Follows only that kind | Yes |
551	| `cursor` | Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer | None, reads the cursor file |
552	| `speaker` | Cuts to whoever is talking in a wide shot | Yes, and the microphones' speech |
553	| `center` | Holds on the middle of the picture | None |
554	| `fit` | Shows the whole picture | None |
555	| `layout` | Lays camera layouts out again on this canvas | None |
556	| `keep` | Rescales the clip from an older canvas | None |
557	
558	The first four rows move the frame over time. The sheets don't offer all of these. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** has Subject, Faces, People, Salient Region and Center, **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** adds Speaker, and Make Vertical uses `cursor`, `fit`, `layout` and `keep` by itself where a clip calls for them. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
559	
560	### `subject`
561	
562	Follows a face. Where there's no face it follows a person, and where there's neither it follows a salient region, the part of the picture that draws the eye. This is **Subject** in [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/), and [How a followed frame moves](#how-a-followed-frame-moves) says what the frame does.
563	
564	### `face`, `person` and `salient`
565	
566	Each follows only that kind. Where there's none to follow, the frame behaves as it does [when a subject is lost](#how-a-followed-frame-moves). These are **Faces**, **People** and **Salient Region** on the Follow Subject sheet.
567	
568	A clip whose media has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) can't use `subject` or these three, because a recording with a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces.
569	
570	### `cursor`
571	
572	Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer, from its media's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). A screen recording made by Frame Job has one.
573	
574	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when the pointer strays more than 20 % of the frame's width, or 12 % of its height, from the middle.
575	- A click outside that area gets there in time: the move ends on the click's frame.
576	- The frame holds still while you type. A click during typing still moves it.
577	
578	It needs no analysis, so it never waits. The frame never shows the whole picture, so `where_empty` and `backdrop` do nothing here.
579	
580	If the cursor file is missing or won't open, the agent is told which file and why. The **Cursor** section of the Media tab has **Locate…** to point the media at a moved file.
581	
582	### `speaker`
583	
584	Frames a wide shot of two to four people on whoever is talking. Each person needs a microphone of their own, and the agent names those clips in `mics`: a clip of a sound file or a camera's detached sound for each, each on its own track.
585	
586	- **Who talks when** is read from the microphones exactly as [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) reads them with its default settings, so the two agree.
587	- **Whose face is whose** comes from matching each microphone to the face whose mouth moves while it talks. Faces are numbered 1, 2 and so on from left to right, and a face has to be in view for at least a quarter of the clip to count.
588	- **Each change of speaker** is a cut, held at least 2 s.
589	- **Two people talking at once** are framed together when they fit. Otherwise the frame stays on whichever of them is already framed, or goes to the first of them in `mics`.
590	- **While nobody talks**, the last speaker stays.
591	
592	**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** has this as Follow **Speaker**, with the microphones and faces confirmed on the sheet. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
593	
594	When the mouths don't move closely enough with the microphones, Frame Job can't tell who is whose. The agent is told where each face is across the picture, for example "face 1 at 28 % across the picture, face 2 at 71 %". It then names each microphone's face in `mic_faces`, in the same order as `mics`, and calls again.
595	
596	Frame Job won't frame on the speaker when:
597	
598	| The problem | What to do |
599	| --- | --- |
600	| `mics` doesn't hold two to four clips, or names a clip twice | Name each microphone once |
601	| A microphone is the clip being framed, or has no sound from a media file | Use a clip of a sound file, or a camera's detached sound |
602	| A microphone's sound is off | Turn it on, or leave it out of `mics` |
603	| Two microphones are on one track | Give each its own track |
604	| `mic_faces` has the wrong count, a face 0, a face twice, or a number past the faces shown | Name one different face for each microphone |
605	| A microphone is still being measured | Try again in a moment. Frame Job measures loudness and speech when a file is added |
606	| A microphone has no speech over the clip | Leave it out, or check it's the right clip |
607	| The clip changes shot | Split it first with [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/) |
608	| Fewer faces show than there are microphones | Use fewer microphones, or a shot that shows everyone |
609	| Nobody speaks inside the clip | Frame the clip another way |
610	
611	`speaker` works on what's open in the window, so a call addressed to a nest that isn't open stops and says to open it with `set_scope` first.
612	
613	### `center`
614	
615	Holds the frame on the middle of the picture for the whole clip. It needs no analysis, and it uses `zoom`.
616	
617	### `fit`
618	
619	Shows the whole picture for the whole clip, scaled to fit the canvas. It needs no analysis and ignores `zoom`. It has no menu choice of its own, but Make Vertical uses it for a recording whose cursor file can't be read.
620	
621	### `layout`
622	
623	Lays a camera clip's [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/), and its screen's, out again on the current canvas, as Make Vertical Version does. The agent can name the camera or the screen, and both change.
624	
625	Frame Job looks at each layout switch made on the old canvas, `from_width` × `from_height`, and works out which layout it was. Its position, crop and corner radius have to match that layout to within 1 px, and its scale and opacity to within 0.001. The switch is then made again on this canvas, at the same time and with the same length and curve. Without those two arguments the old canvas is taken to be the current one.
626	
627	- **Side by Side** becomes **Stacked** on a canvas taller than wide.
628	- The cut pieces of the recording take the new layout.
629	- Any zoom on them is adjusted so it shows the same part of the picture.
630	
631	It ignores `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` and `replace`.
632	
633	Frame Job won't do this for a clip with no camera layout, a clip laid out both as a camera and as a screen, a screen layout with no camera switch in front of it, or a switch edited by hand. The agent is told the clip, and the action when one switch is the problem. For a clip with no layout it can use `subject`, `center`, `fit` or `keep`, and the clip stays as placed until it does.
634	
635	### `keep`
636	
637	Rescales the clip from the canvas it was placed on, `from_width` × `from_height`, to the current one, as `set_canvas` does with `rescale_clips`. Its position follows each axis's change and its scale follows the smaller of the two, and every position and scale its actions set moves with it. Each argument defaults to the current canvas's size, so with neither there's nothing to rescale.
638	
639	It needs no analysis and ignores `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` and `replace`.
640	
641	It works on every clip the other kinds turn down, as long as the clip has a picture. Make Vertical keeps titles, shapes and other clips this way.
642	
643	## How a followed frame moves
644	
645	With `subject`, `face`, `person` and `salient`, the frame:
646	
647	- eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put
648	- cuts with the picture at each shot change, landing on the first frame of the new shot
649	- holds for 1 s when the subject is lost, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing
650	- then follows someone else in the shot, or eases over 0.8 s to what `where_empty` says
651	- comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s
652	- frames two people together when both fit in the frame
653	
654	[How following moves](/framing/follow-subject/#how-following-moves) has the detail.
655	
656	`where_empty` is what the frame shows where there's nothing to follow: `fit`, the whole picture and the default, or `center`, the middle of the picture. These are **Show Whole** and **Center** on the Follow Subject sheet. A clip with nothing to follow anywhere in it shows this for its whole length.
657	
658	## Set how tight the frame is
659	
660	`zoom` is how tight the frame is, from 1 to 4. At 1, the default, the picture is at the scale that fills the canvas. At 2 it's twice that scale.
661	
662	`center`, `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor` and `speaker` use it. A value outside 1 to 4 stops the call whichever kind it asks for.
663	
664	## Put a blurred copy behind the clip
665	
666	Where the framing shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. Name a track behind the clip as `backdrop` and a blurred copy of the clip goes there for the clip's whole length. It's the copy **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
667	
668	- With no `backdrop`, there's no copy.
669	- A copy is made only when the framing shows the whole picture somewhere: with `fit`, or with a followed clip that falls back to the whole picture.
670	- If the named track is locked, a matte, or busy over the clip, the copy goes on a new track at the back instead.
671	- A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.
672	- The result gives the copy's id in `new_clips`, and the track's in `new_tracks` when it needed a new one.
673	
674	## Written as ordinary edits
675	
676	The framing is written as the clip's position and scale, and one action per move, each of which you can change afterwards like any other [action](/motion/actions/). You'll see them on the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/).
677	
678	**Edit ▸ Undo Reframe Clip** takes the whole framing back in one step, and so does the agent's `undo`.
679	
680	## A clip that already has actions
681	
682	A clip keeps the actions it has. The framing is composed into them, so a zoom or pan the clip already makes still happens, inside the new framing, and a volume or speed action still does what it did.
683	
684	The framing's own moves go in the gaps between the clip's actions. A move that would overlap one is moved up to half a second earlier, or else made part of that action, along its curve.
685	
686	A shot change that falls inside an action cuts the action in three around the one-frame cut. A steady change of volume still sounds exactly as it did, and an eased one eases again on each side of the cut. A speed action, or one a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut, and takes the framing's change across its length instead.
687	
688	### Start from the whole picture
689	
690	With `replace` set to true, the framing replaces the clip's own moves instead of working inside them. Every position and scale the clip's actions set is removed, the picture is fitted to the canvas, and then the clip is framed. Volume and everything else stay, and an action left with nothing is removed.
691	
692	The default is false. Every kind uses it but `keep` and `layout`. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** always starts from the whole picture this way, with a **Backgrounds** track as its `backdrop`, as one undo step named **Follow Subject**.
693	
694	## Which options each kind reads
695	
696	| `follow` | `zoom` | `where_empty` | `backdrop` | `replace` | `from_width`, `from_height` |
697	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
698	| `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
699	| `speaker` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
700	| `cursor` | Yes | No | No | Yes | No |
701	| `center` | Yes | No | No | Yes | No |
702	| `fit` | No | No | Yes | Yes | No |
703	| `layout` | No | No | No | No | Yes |
704	| `keep` | No | No | No | No | Yes |
705	
706	`mics` and `mic_faces` belong to `speaker` alone. An option a kind doesn't use is ignored, except that a `zoom` outside 1 to 4, a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0 and an unknown `backdrop` track stop the call whatever the kind.
707	
708	## Waiting for analysis
709	
710	If the part of the file the clip plays hasn't been analysed, the tool analyses it and waits up to a minute. It looks at that part with a second either side, for shots, faces and subjects, on your Mac. In the result, `cached` is false when an analysis ran first. A clip that can't be framed for another reason is turned down straight away, without waiting.
711	
712	If a minute isn't enough, nothing changes and the analysis carries on. The result still says `ok: true`, with an `analyzing` entry naming the files still going and how much is covered, so an agent has to look for it. It then calls again to apply the framing. [The analysis wait](/mcp/tools-framing/#the-analysis-wait) has the details.
713	
714	- `center`, `fit`, `keep`, `cursor` and `layout` need no analysis, so they never wait.
715	- `speaker` also needs its microphones' loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added.
716	- If the project or the open nest changes while the tool reads the analysis, nothing is framed and the agent is told to call again.
717	- If the analysis fails, nothing is framed and the agent is told which analysis and why.
718	- [Stopping the Assistant](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) during the wait frames nothing.
719	
720	## When a clip can't be framed
721	
722	A clip that can't be framed is left as it was, and the agent gets a sentence saying why. Frame Job checks in this order and stops at the first one that applies.
723	
724	| The clip | Which kinds it stops | What still works |
725	| --- | --- | --- |
726	| A text, shape, graphic or adjustment clip | All but `keep` | `keep` |
727	| Has no picture, or a crop or scale leaves none | All | Nothing |
728	| A nest clip, then a still or image clip | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor`, `speaker` | `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
729	| Its media has no cursor file | `cursor` | `subject`, `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
730	| Its media has a cursor file | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `speaker` | `cursor`, `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
731	| On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), or cut by a matte | All but `keep` and `layout` | `keep` |
732	| Turned: a rotation, an action turning it, or a spin in its motion | All but `keep` and `layout` | `keep` |
733	| With a copy to make, a nest clip, or a `backdrop` track that isn't behind the clip's | Any kind that makes a copy | Leave `backdrop` out, or name a track further back |
734	| Analysis holds nothing for the part of the clip that plays, or no recorded pointer falls inside it | `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor` | `center`, `fit`, `keep` |
735	
736	`layout` has [its own checks](#layout), and it skips the matte and turned rows. [`speaker`'s checks](#speaker) come after the turned clip.
737	
738	Before any of that, a call stops on a value it can't use: an unknown clip, track or microphone, a `zoom` outside 1 to 4, or a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0.

16	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
17	
18	Frame Job can find who and what is in a clip's picture: faces, people and the parts the eye goes to first. Its framing tools use this to keep a subject in shot on a canvas of a different shape.
19	
20	<AtAGlance
21	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…', 'View ▸ Show Subjects']}
22	  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
23	  needs="Nothing. Apple's Vision framework does this on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
24	/>
25	
26	## What is found
27	
28	Frame Job samples the picture ten times a second of the file's own time, so a clip you've slowed down or sped up doesn't change what's found. It keeps three things from each sample.
29	
30	### Faces
31	
32	Each face's box, how it's turned, and how open the mouth is. Faces in a sample are listed from left to right. An agent reads them with `get_media_analysis`, kind `faces`. See [Faces](/projects/media-analysis/#faces) under media analysis.
33	
34	### People
35	
36	Each person's head and shoulders, as a box. A person's box can stand in for their face while the face can't be found. An agent reads people with `get_media_analysis`, kind `subjects`.
37	
38	### Salient regions
39	
40	The parts of the picture the eye goes to first, as boxes. In a talking-head shot that's usually the speaker, and on a slide it's often the text. An agent reads them with kind `subjects`, beside the people. See [People and salient regions](/projects/media-analysis/#people-and-salient-regions) under media analysis.
41	
42	[Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) draws all three over the preview, so you can see what Frame Job has to work with.
43	
44	## Boxes, not people
45	
46	Each sample stands alone. A box has no name, and nothing records that a box in one sample is the same person as a box in the next. Frame Job never puts a name to a face, and it doesn't recognise anyone.
47	
48	[Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/#which-subject-it-follows) works out who's who for itself each time, from how the boxes overlap from one sample to the next. That reasoning isn't kept, and it stops at a shot change. Someone who leaves the shot for more than a second and comes back counts as someone new.
49	
50	## When a file is analysed
51	
52	Importing a file doesn't look for any of this. It's found when something asks for it:
53	
54	- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**
55	- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**
56	- [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/one-microphone/), when it cuts from faces
57	- An agent, with `get_media_analysis`, `reframe_clip`, `make_vertical_version` or `switch_by_speaker`
58	
59	Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and `reframe_clip` ask only for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side. **View ▸ Show Subjects** never asks, so turning it on costs nothing.
60	
61	Analysis runs in the background and saves what it has found every 30 seconds, so stopping it keeps what's been saved. Asking again continues from there, and a part that's already been analysed isn't read again. What's found is kept in the project's cache. A change to the file, or a macOS update, means it's analysed again.
62	
63	[On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-happens-on-demand) covers this in full, along with everything else Frame Job analyses on your Mac, including [the Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) and [how background jobs run](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-runs-in-the-background).
64

73	| [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) | All three, drawn over the preview |

91	Show Subjects outlines what Frame Job has found in the selected clip at the playhead, right on the preview. Use it to check what [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) has to work with.
92	
93	<AtAGlance
94	  menu="View ▸ Show Subjects"

98	## Turn on Show Subjects
99	
100	<Steps>
101	
102	1. Select a clip of a movie.
103	
104	2. Move the playhead to a moment that clip shows.
105	
106	3. Choose **View ▸ Show Subjects**. A tick appears beside it in the menu.
107	
108	</Steps>
109	
110	If a note appears instead of boxes, the clip hasn't been analysed yet. See [Not analyzed](#not-analyzed).
111	
112	Select another clip to see its boxes, and move the playhead to see another moment. Choose the item again to turn it off.
113	
114	The item has no shortcut, and it's available whenever the window has no sheet open.
115	
116	It draws for one clip at a time. With several clips selected, that's the front-most one showing at the playhead. A selected still, picture, nest, text, shape or graphic draws nothing and shows no note, and neither does a clip the playhead isn't on.
117	
118	## What the outlines mean
119	
120	| Outline | What it marks |
121	| --- | --- |
122	| Yellow | A face |
123	| Teal | A person's head and shoulders |
124	| Purple, dashed | A salient region, a part of the picture the eye goes to first |
125	
126	Each outline has a dark line behind it, so it stays visible on a bright picture. Faces draw on top of the other two.
127	
128	[Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) explains what each kind of box is.
129	
130	## The boxes stay on the picture
131	
132	The boxes sit on the clip's picture wherever you've placed it. If you've moved, scaled or rotated the clip, each box moves and turns with it. If you've cropped the clip, the boxes are clipped to the crop.
133	
134	They also follow the clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal, so they show what the clip is showing at that moment rather than what's at the same time in the file.
135	
136	## Not analyzed
137	
138	When nothing has been found for the clip's picture at the playhead, a note sits at the clip's top-left corner:
139	
140	> Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it
141	
142	Show Subjects never starts an analysis, so turning it on costs nothing. To make the boxes, run [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) or [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) on the clip. If Show Subjects is on when an analysis lands, the boxes appear by themselves.
143	
144	Three situations are worth knowing:
145	
146	- Analysis covers the parts of a file that clips play, plus a second either side. Another part of the same file can still read "Not analyzed".
147	- A part that's been analysed and holds nothing shows no outlines and no note.
148	- Follow Subject doesn't analyse a screen recording that has its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), so the note stays on such a clip. See [Screen recordings are skipped](/framing/follow-subject/#screen-recordings-are-skipped).
149	
150	## A view of the window
151	
152	Show Subjects belongs to the window, not the project. It's off in a new window, each window has its own setting, and it isn't remembered between launches. It edits nothing, so it isn't an undo step, and it never changes an export or a saved frame.
153	
154	## With an agent
155	
156	There's no agent tool for the overlay. An agent reads the same boxes with [`get_media_analysis`](/mcp/tools-analysis/#get_media_analysis).
